title: Local strictly henselian structure of the finite-lift colimit
statement:
Let $(H,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a commutative henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], with residue field $k$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $K/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $I$ be the small directed poset of finite separable intermediate fields of $K/k$. Suppose given a diagram $(B_e,u_{ef})_{e\in I}$ of finite local etale $H$-algebras [def-weil-etale-morphism], with maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_e=\mathfrak mB_e$, local structure maps and local transitions, together with compatible $k$-algebra isomorphisms $r_e:B_e/\mathfrak n_e\xrightarrow{\sim}e$ inducing the inclusions $e\subset f$ on residues. There exists a colimit $C$ in commutative $H$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and every such colimit with coprojections $\iota_e$ is also the colimit of the underlying commutative-ring diagram. The compatible maps $B_e\to e\hookrightarrow K$ induce a surjection $q:C\to K$ with
$$\ker q=\bigcup_{e\in I}\iota_e(\mathfrak n_e).$$
Every element of $C$ has a representative in some $B_e$, and every element outside $\ker q$ is a unit. The ring $C$ is local with maximal ideal $\ker q$, every $\iota_e$ and $H\to C$ is local, and $q$ identifies $C/\mathfrak m_C$ with $K$ as a $k$-algebra. Each $B_e$ is henselian, $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ is a henselian pair, and $C$ is strictly henselian. Moreover $H\to C$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. No Noetherian or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The given poset $I$ is small and directed, hence filtered and nonempty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist] with $R=H$ to obtain an algebra colimit. For any such colimit $(C,\iota_e)$, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] makes its underlying ring cocone a colimit and gives a representative $c=\iota_e(b)$ for every $c\in C$. These conclusions apply to every algebra-colimit cocone, not only a chosen construction.

For each $e$, let $q_e:B_e\to K$ be reduction modulo $\mathfrak n_e$, followed by $r_e$ and $e\hookrightarrow K$. Compatibility of the $r_e$ gives $q_f u_{ef}=q_e$. The ring-colimit universal property gives a unique $q:C\to K$ with $q\iota_e=q_e$. Every $z\in K$ lies in the finite separable subfield $k(z)$ since $K/k$ is algebraic separable; surjectivity of reduction and of $r_{k(z)}$ gives a preimage of $z$ in $B_{k(z)}$, and hence in $C$. For $c=\iota_e(b)$, injectivity of $r_e$ and $e\hookrightarrow K$ gives $q(c)=0$ if and only if $b\in\mathfrak n_e$. Thus $q$ is surjective and $M:=\ker q=\bigcup_e\iota_e(\mathfrak n_e)$.

source.place: Tag 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h), residue field sentence, with the residue map and kernel made explicit

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-colimit-residue-field] to the underlying ring colimit: the diagram consists of local rings and all transitions are local by hypothesis, and $I$ is nonempty, small and directed. Its unique maximal ideal is the union computed in Step 2, namely $M$, and $\iota_e^{-1}(M)=\mathfrak n_e$. In particular all $\iota_e$ are local. If $c=\iota_e(b)\notin M$, then $b\notin\mathfrak n_e$ and the local-ring unit criterion gives $bd=1$ in $B_e$ for some $d$. Thus $c\iota_e(d)=1$, proving the asserted unit clause. Choose any $e\in I$: since $H\to B_e$ is local, the inverse image of $M$ under $H\to B_e\to C$ is $\mathfrak m$. Hence $H\to C$ is local.

source.place: Tag 04GI (lemma-colimit-henselian), omitted local-ring argument, and Tag 0BSL

proof.text: The map $[c]\mapsto q(c)$ from $C/M$ to $K$ is well defined, injective by $M=\ker q$, and surjective by Step 2; it is therefore a ring isomorphism. For $h\in H$ and any $e$, $q(\iota_e(h))$ is the image in $K$ of the residue of $h$ in $k$, because $r_e$ is a $k$-algebra isomorphism. The displayed isomorphism is thus a $k$-algebra isomorphism for the residue $k$-algebra structure on $C/M$. Step 3 identifies $M$ with $\mathfrak m_C$, so this is exactly the required residue-field identification.

For each $e$, the ring $H$ is henselian local, $B_e$ is local, and $B_e$ is finite as an $H$-module by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-henselian] with $R=H$, $A=B_e$. This proves that every $B_e$ is henselian. By the meaning of henselian local ring, each pair $(B_e,\mathfrak n_e)$ is consequently henselian.

source.place: Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian), part (2); Tag 0BSL, henselianity of the finite lifts

proof.text: The transitions send $\mathfrak n_e$ into $\mathfrak n_f$ because they are local. Thus the pairs of Step 5 form a directed system of henselian pairs. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-henselian-pair] to the ring colimit of Step 1. It yields a henselian pair $(C,\bigcup_e\iota_e(\mathfrak n_e))=(C,M)$. By Step 3, $M=\mathfrak m_C$, so $C$ is henselian local. By Step 4 its residue field is $K$, which is separably closed since it is a separable closure of $k$. The definition of strictly henselian now gives that $C$ is strictly henselian.

source.place: Tag 0FWT (lemma-filtered-colimits-henselian), applied to the maximal-ideal pairs; algebra.tex Tag 0BSL, strictly henselian conclusion

proof.text: Each term $B_e$ is an etale $H$-algebra, hence of finite presentation as part of the etale hypothesis. The given small directed diagram and the algebra colimit of Step 1 therefore exhibit $C$ as a filtered colimit of etale $H$-algebras of finite presentation. This is precisely the defining condition for $H\to C$ to be ind-etale. All arguments used only the stated hypotheses; none used Noetherianity or completeness.

lean.statement: theorem finite_local_lift_colimit_structure (H K : Type u) [CommRing H] [HenselianLocalRing H] [Field K] [Algebra (ResidueField H) K] [IsSepClosure (ResidueField H) K] (B : {e : IntermediateField (ResidueField H) K // FiniteDimensional (ResidueField H) e ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable (ResidueField H) e} ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u} H) [∀ e, IsLocalRing (B.obj e)] [∀ e, Module.Finite H (B.obj e)] [∀ e, Algebra.Etale H (B.obj e)] [∀ e, IsLocalHom (algebraMap H (B.obj e))] [∀ (e f) (a : e ⟶ f), IsLocalHom (B.map a).hom.toRingHom] (hn : ∀ e, maximalIdeal (B.obj e) = Ideal.map (algebraMap H (B.obj e)) (maximalIdeal H)) (r : ∀ e, ResidueField (B.obj e) ≃+* e.1) (hr_base : ∀ e, (r e).toRingHom.comp (ResidueField.map (algebraMap H (B.obj e))) = algebraMap (ResidueField H) e.1) (hr_transition : ∀ (e f) (a : e ⟶ f) (b : B.obj e), ((r f) (residue (B.obj f) ((B.map a).hom b)) : K) = ((r e) (residue (B.obj e) b) : K)) : Nonempty (ColimitCocone B) ∧ ∀ (c : Cocone B), IsColimit c → Nonempty (IsColimit ((forget₂ (CommAlgCat H) CommRingCat).mapCocone c)) ∧ ∃ q : c.pt →+* K, (∀ e, ∀ b : B.obj e, q ((c.ι.app e).hom b) = ((r e) (residue (B.obj e) b) : K)) ∧ Function.Surjective q ∧ (RingHom.ker q : Set c.pt) = (⋃ e, (c.ι.app e).hom '' (maximalIdeal (B.obj e) : Set (B.obj e))) ∧ (∀ x : c.pt, ∃ e, ∃ b : B.obj e, (c.ι.app e).hom b = x) ∧ (∀ x : c.pt, x ∉ RingHom.ker q → IsUnit x) ∧ ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing c.pt) (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap H c.pt)), maximalIdeal c.pt = RingHom.ker q ∧ (∀ e, IsLocalHom (c.ι.app e).hom.toRingHom) ∧ (∃ rC : ResidueField c.pt ≃+* K, (∀ x : c.pt, rC (residue c.pt x) = q x) ∧ rC.toRingHom.comp (ResidueField.map (algebraMap H c.pt)) = algebraMap (ResidueField H) K) ∧ (∀ e, HenselianLocalRing (B.obj e)) ∧ HenselianRing c.pt (maximalIdeal c.pt) ∧ IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing c.pt ∧ RingHom.IndEtaleAcrossUniverses (algebraMap H c.pt)
